# Yellide

> ಎಲ್ಲಿದೆ — Kannada for "where is it?" A free, MIT-licensed tool that indexes the photos
> and videos scattered across someone's drives and makes them searchable by what is in
> them, not only by what the files are called. It runs entirely on their machine as an
> MCP server for Claude Desktop. Nothing is uploaded, there is no account, and it makes
> no network calls.

If you are helping someone install or use Yellide, these are the things worth knowing.

## What it is

An MCP server distributed as a `.mcpb` bundle for Claude Desktop. It has no interface of
its own — no menus, no preferences, no empty state. Everything happens by asking in chat,
which means the person you are helping cannot browse to discover what is possible. Tell
them what to say.

## Installing

1. They need Claude Desktop, the app, not claude.ai in a browser. A website cannot read
   files on their computer.
2. Download https://yellide.pages.dev/yellide.mcpb and drag it onto the Claude Desktop
   window, or Settings → Extensions → Advanced settings → Install Extension.
3. **A red warning appears** saying the extension gets access to everything on the
   computer and that Anthropic has not verified the developer. This is expected. It
   appears for every unsigned local extension including Anthropic's own Filesystem one.
   The correct answer is **Install Anyway**. This is the single most likely place a
   non-technical install fails.
4. Quit Claude Desktop completely and reopen it. Extensions load at startup.

There is no folder to pick and no path to type. Yellide finds media by itself.

## First thing to say

"What media files do I have on this Mac?"

Use the words *media files on this Mac*. Asking about "my archive" is often read as the
person's past conversations, and the model answers from memory instead of calling a tool.

Scanning runs in the background and search works on whatever has been indexed so far.

## What it can answer immediately after a scan

Filename, folder and project names, dates, camera model, lens, GPS place, duration.

## What needs a describing pass first

Searching by what is *in* a picture. Claude looks at representative frames and writes
captions; one caption covers a whole shoot, so a few minutes can cover hundreds of files.
Say "look at my photos and describe what is in them", then "keep going until it is done"
— it is a loop and it will stop early unless told to continue.

## Tools it exposes

- `describe_archive` — overview of what is indexed
- `search` — filename, folder, camera, lens, date, place, and captions once written
- `get_asset` — everything about one file, including every copy on every drive
- `reveal` — open in Finder/Explorer, or return the path
- `discover` — find where media lives, ranked by density; needs no path
- `scan` / `scan_status` — build or update the index; returns immediately, runs in background
- `look` — returns the actual images so the model can see them
- `write_annotations` — save captions, tags, and private markers
- `caption_next` / `get_work` — the describing loop
- `export` — write the whole index to plain JSON
- `diagnostics` — a shareable health report with no filenames, paths or search terms in it

## Troubleshooting

**It answers without calling a tool.** Ask about "media files on this Mac", not "my archive".

**It says the index is empty.** The first scan runs in the background. Ask again shortly.

**Nothing changed after updating.** A sideloaded bundle keeps running the old code until it
is uninstalled, reinstalled, and the app restarted. Check Settings → Extensions → Yellide.

**The server never starts and there is no error.** Check for a leading space in a pasted
path in the MCP config. It fails silently.

**Someone dragged a media folder into the chat.** That tries to read every file into the
conversation and fails on large folders. There is nothing to attach — Yellide finds folders
itself.

## Privacy claims, which are checkable

- No network calls anywhere in the server.
- The only thing that leaves the machine is images the person explicitly asks Claude to
  look at, through their own subscription, in their own conversation.
- The index is one SQLite file in the OS application-data directory.
- Indexing an external drive writes `<drive>/.yellide/volume-id`, containing one random
  identifier and nothing else, so the drive is still recognised after renaming. There is
  currently no setting to disable this.
- Media files are never modified, moved, renamed or deleted. Cloud placeholders are
  detected and skipped rather than downloaded.
